newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy-short-term rates near 3-pct is positive.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy-short-term rates near 3-pct is positive.

text.p: Alexandre Lamfalussy, the outgoing president of the European Monetary Institute, said on Monday that monetary policy can help contribute to balanced growth but that there is currently only limited room for manouevre in the run-up to Europe's currency union.

"Once inflation has been brought under control, and once this control has been confirmed, monetary policy can guide short-term interest rates to a level which contributes to balanced growth," he said in a speech at a ceremony to turn over the presidency to Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg.
"Quite a number of EU countries are in such a situation already, with short-term interest rates around three percent," Lamfalussy added.

At the same time, Lamfalussy said "nominal long-term interest rates are at a historically low level - they are well below six percent - but real long-term interest rates can be regarded, perhaps, as still being too high to put continental Europe on the road to more vigorous growth."

Lamfalussy expressed doubt whether still looser monetary policy in Europe would be successful in moving the yield curve in the desired direction, rather he said such moves might actually have the opposite effects.
"In any event, given the current level of short-term interest rates, monetary policy's margin for manoeuvre is extremely limited," Lamfalussy said.

Noting that government debt has risen not fallen in the past years, Lamfalussy worried "this development, together with the worry that it might not yet have run its course, are not likely - to say the least - to lead to a fall in real interest rates."
At the same time, this development does not create the "climate of confidence necessary for consumers and investors to modify their prudent behaviour," Lamfalussy added.

Noting that Europe's most pressing problem is its stubbornly high unemployment rates, Lamfalussy said "stronger growth would certainly have a beneficial effect on employment," stressing however it would not eliminate the structural component of the employment problem.
